# Access, Session & Security Requirements Quality Checklist: SPEC 002

**Purpose**: Formal pre-`/speckit-tasks` gate — validate that the authentication,
session-lifecycle, route-protection, and access-security requirements in the
SPEC 002 spec are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before tasks are
derived.
**Created**: 2026-09-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/auth-and-session.md](../contracts/auth-and-session.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Evaluation history**:
- **2026-09-11 (pass 1, pre-implementation review)**: assessed every CHK against the current spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md and tasks.md. **19 satisfied, 5 gaps (0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 5 LOW)**. No functional scope was changed; no new tasks were required. Gate: **ABIERTA (open) — sin HIGH/MEDIUM pendientes.**

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the final wording of the generic authentication error message defined, or does FR-004 leave it as an example ("por ejemplo, «Usuario o contraseña incorrectos.»")? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking — same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK002): FR-004 and `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §F4 both keep the string as "p. ej." (example). The exact prose isn't spec-mandated, but the message is pinned to a single fixed content constant (`idaf.auth.invalidCredentials`) and its load-bearing property (does not name the failed field) is tested. The literal wording is an implementation detail of `content/idaf.ts`.

- [x] CHK002 Does the spec state, as a traceable FR or SC, that credentials/secrets must not appear in source code, logs, the delivered bundle, or the interface — or does that requirement live only in the Dependencies section? [Traceability, Spec §Dependencies, §FR-005]
  - PASS: FR-055 plus SC-025/SC-026 (added in the 2026-09-08 clarification session) now state this explicitly as first-class FR/SC, not only as a Dependencies note.

- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for the case where the authentication mechanism itself is unavailable or errors, as distinct from invalid credentials? [Coverage, Gap]
  - PASS: FR-056 + SC-027 + CL-09 fully specify this distinct case (a `503`/error-of-verification path, distinguishable message, no session created).

- [x] CHK004 Is the minimum (and any maximum) number of predefined accounts specified, rather than "varias cuentas distintas"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-052]
  - PASS: FR-052 states "al menos dos" as an explicit minimum. No maximum is defined, which is intentional — the set is open-ended by design (plan.md Scale/Scope gives an indicative, non-binding 2–10 range at the implementation level).

- [x] CHK005 Does the spec define what IDAF shows when an already-authenticated user opens the login route? [Coverage, Gap; Spec §FR-003, §FR-053]
  - PASS: FR-057 + SC-028 + CL-10 (added in the 2026-09-08 clarification) fully specify this: redirect to Inicio, no second form, session not closed.

- [ ] CHK006 Are transport-confidentiality expectations for submitted credentials stated or explicitly deferred, given the spec scope is "acceso mediante autenticación"? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): no spec-level FR/SC addresses transport confidentiality. `data-model.md` §1 mentions "HTTPS en despliegue" only as a plan-level aside, not elevated to a spec requirement or an explicit Out-of-Scope entry. Practically mitigated by same-origin delivery (Vite proxy, contract §A5.3) but not spec-traceable.

- [x] CHK007 Is a requirement stated for where keyboard focus goes on a failed login attempt, given FR-054 only covers "al iniciar y al cerrar sesión"? [Coverage, Gap; Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS (resolved in current spec): current FR-054 text explicitly adds the failure case ("cuando el inicio de sesión falla … al mensaje de error o permanece en el formulario de acceso"), added in the 2026-09-08 clarification session. The gap this item describes no longer exists.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is the empty-field indication of FR-006 / CL-01 distinguished from the generic invalid-credentials message of FR-004 — specifically, may the empty-field message name which field is missing without violating FR-005? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-004, §FR-005, §CL-01]
  - PASS: FR-005 is explicitly scoped to "el mensaje de error de autenticación" (FR-004's post-submission message), not to FR-006's separate client-side field-required check. `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §F2 confirms the empty-field hint is shown **without ever calling** `login()` — a structurally distinct code path from the generic invalid-credentials message, so naming the empty field there does not implicate FR-005.

- [ ] CHK009 Is "la sesión sobrevive solo a la recarga de página" precise enough to distinguish a page reload from browser session-restore reopening the tab/window? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-051, §CL-08]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): research D3's rejected-alternative note acknowledges that "algunas configuraciones restauran pestañas con la cookie viva" but frames the `sessionStorage` marker as resolving "pestaña cerrada" generally; browser-specific "continue where you left off" session restore can, in some browsers, also restore `sessionStorage`, which the design doesn't explicitly reconcile. Edge case, not addressed with certainty either way.

- [x] CHK010 Is "la sesión DEBE finalizar de inmediato" expressed as an observable condition (e.g., protected routes unreachable without re-authentication right after logout)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013]
  - PASS: `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §A3.1 makes it observable — session deletion is synchronous and a subsequent `GET /session` on the same cookie immediately returns `{authenticated:false}`; SC-004 tests the user-facing consequence.

- [x] CHK011 Is "identificación comprensible del usuario autenticado" bounded to the displayed name/identifier only, and stated consistently between FR-011 and the Assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §Assumptions]
  - PASS: FR-011's parenthetical ("al menos su nombre o identificador") and the Assumptions bullet ("no se requieren avatar, correo, rol ni datos de perfil") state the same bound consistently.

- [x] CHK012 Is "presentarse agrupadas … separadas visualmente de la navegación" (FR-015) given any checkable property, or is it validated only through the user-confusion outcome in SC-009? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015, §SC-009]
  - PASS: beyond the SC-009 behavioral outcome, `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §3 N8 and §4 give a structural, checkable property — `SessionBar` and `PrimaryNav` occupy distinct landmark regions (`banner` vs. `navigation`).

- [x] CHK013 Is "credenciales válidas" defined (exact match of username + password against a predefined set) with the matching rules that determine validity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §Key Entities]
  - PASS: `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §A1.1 and `data-model.md` §1 both state the exact matching rule (`username` case-sensitive match + `timingSafeEqual(scrypt(password, salt), passwordHash)`).

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 Are FR-008 (direct access without session → login) and FR-014 (post-logout protected access → login) non-redundant, or is one fully entailed by the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-014]
  - PASS: both requirements resolve to the same underlying guard (`RequireSession`, contract §E1) and are deliberately kept as distinct requirements for scenario/test traceability (`contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §2 R1 vs. R4) rather than being in conflict — a harmless, intentional redundancy.

- [ ] CHK015 Do FR-001/FR-008/FR-010 (no session) and FR-009/FR-053 (active session) jointly cover every {route category × session state} combination without contradiction? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, FR-008, FR-009, FR-010, FR-053]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): every combination is covered except one — "unknown route (`*`) while anonymous" is only made explicit in `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §2 R6 (inferred from FR-008/FR-001, since the guard fires uniformly regardless of route validity), not spelled out verbatim in the spec's FR text. Behavior is tested (`tests/e2e/unknown-route.spec.ts`, tasks.md T074), so this is a documentation gap, not a functional one.

- [x] CHK016 Is "todos los usuarios autenticados DEBEN tener la misma experiencia" (FR-016) consistent with FR-052's requirement that each account has its own displayed name/identifier? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, §FR-052]
  - PASS: FR-052 explicitly cross-references FR-016 ("Todas las cuentas DEBEN tener la misma experiencia (ver FR-016)") — display identity and functional experience are clearly reconciled as orthogonal axes.

- [x] CHK017 Is reload-with-session behavior (FR-009: stay in the same section) consistent with the "exactly one active module" rule (FR-022) during the interval before the section is restored? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §FR-022]
  - PASS: `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §E1 renders a minimal neutral placeholder during `loading` — no nav and no area content is mounted — so FR-022's "exactly one active" invariant has no opportunity to be violated during the transient window; it applies only once `PrimaryNav` is actually mounted.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for multiple concurrent tabs/windows (e.g., logging out in one tab while another still shows an authenticated view)? [Coverage, Gap]
  - PASS: FR-058 + SC-029 + CL-11 (added in the 2026-09-08 clarification session) fully specify this scenario.

- [x] CHK019 Is the post-N-failed-attempts behavior fully specified as "no change, no lockout", and is the absence of throttling/attempt-logging/telemetry an explicit, traceable exclusion? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §CL-02, §Assumptions]
  - PASS: FR-007/CL-02 state the "no lockout" rule; the Assumptions bullet and §Out of Scope explicitly exclude attempt-logging/telemetry and account lockout by name.

- [x] CHK020 Are recovery expectations defined when a session is presumed active but is no longer valid (e.g., the account was removed from the predefined set), so the user lands on login rather than a broken state? [Recovery, Gap; Spec §FR-051]
  - PASS: `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §A2.1 and `data-model.md` §3 specify the general fallback — an unrecognized/invalid session resolves to `{authenticated:false}` → client state `anonymous` → login, generalizing the same rule FR-001 already applies. Account-catalog mutability itself is explicitly out of scope, so no dedicated spec-level FR is needed beyond this general rule.

- [x] CHK021 Is "acceso directo a una ruta … sin sesión" (FR-008) specified to cover both typed URLs and in-app deep links, and is the resulting screen the login (not the requested section)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008]
  - PASS: FR-008 explicitly states the outcome is "la pantalla de acceso, no a la sección solicitada", and the mechanism (`RequireSession` guarding every protected route regardless of how it was reached) is inherently agnostic to typed URL vs. deep link.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK022 Does SC-002's "menos de 30 segundos" state whether it measures user task-completion time or system response time, and the starting event? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
  - PASS: spec §Evaluación con personas → «Medición de tiempos» gives explicit t0/t1 events and instrument for SC-002 (test-runner timestamp).

- [ ] CHK023 Are the "100 % de las veces/intentos" targets in SC-001, SC-003, SC-004, SC-005, and SC-024 backed by a defined number of trials or a defined set of conditions? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003, §SC-004, §SC-005, §SC-024]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking — same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK017): deterministic SCs run once per browser × 3 (quickstart §4/§6), authoritative for a deterministic assertion; there is no general "N attempts" trial count backing the "100%" phrasing, which is cosmetic for checks with no source of randomness.

- [x] CHK024 Is SC-009 ("cero personas confunden «Cerrar sesión»") backed by a defined test method (participant count, task, pass threshold)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009]
  - PASS: spec §Rúbrica de SC-009 gives an observable behavior list (a)–(c), a ≥5-evaluator panel, and a 100%-pass threshold.
